title: scat machine interface, schema_version 2
description: The one JSON document a scat command prints with --json, and the dict a Python result's to_dict() returns. Every object allows extra fields: adding a field does not change schema_version. The set of rule ids is not enumerated here, only its pattern. Version 2 follows the layout of D-088: pages are group, concern, affordance, technology and narrative; an edge is a row of a narrative table, so record-edge and remove-edge results name the edge and the rows they touched. kind is check, status, operation or view. A refusal, even by check or status, gives kind operation with ok false. ok is false on an error or a refusal; warnings keep it true. The exit code is 0 when ok, 1 otherwise, and 2 for a command line that cannot be read. Stdout holds exactly one document; text for humans goes to stderr. Line numbers count the file's lines, front matter included; columns count characters, from 1.

OperationName.description: The command name as typed after scat (check, status, set-status, index, stub, stub-links, record-edge, remove-edge, fingerprint, edges, layered, trace, export-edges). New commands may appear, so the names are not enumerated.

VaultPath.description: Vault-relative, / separators: no leading slash, no backslash, no .. segment.

RuleId.description: Stable: never renamed, only retired. The set grows without a version bump.

AnyPathList.description: export-edges and draw only: a path inside the vault is vault-relative with /; a folder outside it is written as given.

CheckResult.description: What check returns when it ran. A check that could not run (not a vault, page not found, ...) is an OperationResult with ok false.

ok.description: False when any problem has severity error; warnings alone keep it true. The exit code encodes the same boolean.

StatusResult.description: What status returns when it ran. A status that could not run is an OperationResult with ok false.

scope.description: page: one page. neighborhood: a page and its linked pages. vault: every page.

counts.description: Pages per status. Besides the statuses of the ontology, other is a missing or invalid status. Every page type carries a status, so there is no count for pages without one (version 1 had none, for class pages).

type.description: The type key as written; null when there is none that is a string.

status.description: The status as written; null when missing or not a string.

OperationResult.description: What every other command returns, and what check and status return when they refuse. ok is true exactly when refused is empty. created holds pages the call wrote new (for record-edge and remove-edge, the stub of a missing end node or narrative); changed, pages it altered (for those two, the narratives it wrote a row into); notes, sentences for a person. Links are never added or removed by record-edge or remove-edge.

unchanged.description: Looked at and already right: nothing written.

problems.description: Optional. The problems the write leaves, on the pages it touched and the pages one link away, in the catalogue's sort order.

rows_added.description: The rows the call wrote. Both rows_added and rows_removed are empty when the call found nothing to do: ok is then true and the narratives are in unchanged.

allOf.description: Every operation but export-edges and draw lists vault paths.
record-edge and remove-edge, when they ran, name the edge and the rows they added and removed. When they refuse, nothing was written and these fields may be absent.

ViewNode.description: A node of a view: a page of one of the four layers.

type.description: The layer, in layer order: group, concern, affordance, technology.

ViewEdge.description: An edge of the graph, one per (type, from, to), as every view gives it: with every narrative that tells it, and its derived status (the least advanced of those narratives). Relationship annotations appear in no view.

ViewCandidate.description: A rule-4 candidate (D-085): two nodes a narrative links, with an edge type between their layers, and no row. It is not an edge.

ViewNarrative.description: One narrative's fingerprint: nodes flat in layer order then name; edges are the narrative's own rows; candidates are linked pairs that have no row, present only when the view was asked for them (absent by default).

ViewResult.description: What fingerprint, edges, layered and trace return when they ran: the data of one view, deterministic (layer order, then name; edges in graph order; narratives in path order). A view that cannot run (unknown name, an error in a page it draws, no vault) is an OperationResult with ok false and its problems. fingerprint: narratives. edges: edge_type, from_layer, to_layer, rows. layered: narratives (names), nodes (by layer), edges. trace: node, direction, up and down (nodes in layer order then name; empty for a direction not asked), edges (those walked); the node itself is in neither list.

narratives.description: fingerprint: the fingerprints (ViewNarrative), one per narrative asked, or every narrative in path order. layered: the names of the narratives drawn.

rows.description: edges: every edge of the type, in graph order.

nodes.description: layered: the nodes the fingerprints link, keyed by layer, in layer order.

subject.description: The file, field or name the refusal is about.

rule.description: Optional. The rule of the catalogue that gives the refusal (SCAT-DONE-REFUSED for a refusal to set a page to done; that refusal's own fix has two options: an advisory one, and set-status <page> draft as an exact command). A refusal of record-edge or remove-edge (a narrative it would change is done, an unknown type, ends in the wrong layers) writes nothing, and edge, rows_added and rows_removed may then be absent.

problems.description: Optional. The problems that make the refusal, as they stand in the situation the operation judged (for SCAT-DONE-REFUSED, the errors the page would have at status done), each with its fix.

EdgeType.description: The slug of an edge type, as the ontology states it (scat:slug). For remove-edge, the type its ends' layers fix. A closed list: a new edge type bumps schema_version.

EdgeRef.description: An edge of the knowledge graph, as record-edge and remove-edge leave it: one per (type, from, to).

from.description: The page name of the node at the first end.

to.description: The page name of the node at the second end.

narratives.description: The page names of every narrative that has a row for this edge once the operation is done, in byte order. Empty after a remove-edge that took the last row: the edge is gone from the graph.

RowRef.description: One row of a narrative's table of edges that an operation added or removed.

narrative.description: The page name of the narrative.

line.description: The line of the row: in the file as written, for an added row; in the file as it was before the write, for a removed row.

note.description: The row's note cell, as written (empty when there is none).

line.description: From 1, counting the file's lines, front matter included. For a problem about a table, the line of the row (of the header row, for the header).

column.description: From 1, counting characters. For a problem about a table, the first character of the cell it is about (of the first |, for a whole row).

field.description: The field the problem is about: a front-matter field of the page, or a key of scat.toml (then file is scat.toml); null when it is about a link, a table or one of its rows, the whole front matter, a name, and so on.

where.description: Where in the file, for example row 2 cell `to`. A row is removed by a delete-line edit; a cell is corrected by a replace-text edit with a column.

text.description: The whole message exactly as scat check prints it, fix included.

kind.description: The kind of the catalogue rule's fix. Each option has its own kind (never options). exact carries a command, edits or both; slot has an author_slot on an edit or on its command; advisory and manual carry neither.

head.description: The line that introduces the options, for example Fix, choose one:

sequence.description: True: do every option in order (steps). Absent or false: the options are alternatives; the author picks one.

options.description: Alternatives unless sequence is true. An option applies its edits, then its command.

text.description: The sentence shown today. A slot option may be a choice among exact values (no author_slot), such as the missing timeframe of a page (SCAT-DONE-FIELD); an option may only add (a suggestion you confirm) without clearing the problem on its own: read this text.

edits.description: Apply in order, then run command if there is one. In a fix with sequence true, each option is one step.

argv.description: The scat command line as an argument list, without the leading scat.

repl.description: The same call in the Python REPL.

author_slot.description: Present when argv holds a placeholder the author must replace: this is that placeholder's exact text. Never run it as is.

Edit.description: One change a tool can apply. A closed list of actions; a new action bumps schema_version (delete-line, new in version 2, is how a table row is removed).

SetField.description: Set a front-matter field to value (add the field when absent, replace it otherwise). On scat.toml, a top-level key. A list value is the whole new list. Edits are computed from the file as checked, so two set-field fixes for one field do not compose: apply one, then re-check.

value.description: A JSON value; the tool writing it chooses the YAML or TOML spelling. When the page has no front matter, add a block between two --- lines. Also used for a key of scat.toml.

author_slot.description: Present when value holds a placeholder the author must replace: this is that placeholder's exact text. Never write it as is. In an array value, the placeholder is the text of one string element.

DeleteField.description: Delete a front-matter field and its value.

ReplaceText.description: Replace the text find with replace on a line of the page (its body, or front matter lines that are not a plain field). find is the literal text as written in the file at that line. Without column, find is replaced everywhere on the line; with column, only the occurrence at that column. replace may contain a line break, which adds a line (a table's separator row is added this way; for a new table, anchor on the last line of the file; no catalogue fix inserts a row); a fix then has no other edit to a later line of the same file.

author_slot.description: Present when replace holds a placeholder the author must replace: this is that placeholder's exact text. Never write it as is.

column.description: Where find starts on the line. Present: only the occurrence at this column is replaced. Absent: every occurrence on the line is.

DeleteLine.description: Delete one whole line of the page, with its line break. Used to remove a row of a narrative's table: a line cannot be removed by replace-text, which would leave an empty line, and an empty line ends a table. find is the whole line as written, a guard: when the line at line is not exactly find, nothing is deleted.

find.description: The whole line as written, without its line break.

RenameFile.description: Rename a file. Links that named it are not rewritten by this edit.
